one_liner: Senior VA contracting officer who buys supplies and services under the FAR, negotiates and administers contracts, and mentors other Contract Specialists, working on site.
fit_summary: This GS-13 1102 job requires 4 years of contracting experience, 1 year at GS-12 level doing technical contract reviews, a bachelor's degree with 24 semester hours in business-related fields, and a contracting warrant within about 6 months. Daniel's IEM consulting background and policy knowledge don't show hands-on federal procurement work on file, so this only works if Daniel's IEM role actually involved contract management, proposals, pricing, or audits at a senior level.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens) and to displaced federal employees under CTAP/ICTAP; no federal status is needed.

1102 basic requirements: at least 4 years of contracting or related experience, plus a 4-year bachelor's course of study that included at least 24 semester hours in accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, industrial management, marketing, quantitative methods, or organization and management.
One year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-12, such as technical contract reviews, interpreting regulations, trend reports, and coordinating audit responses.
You must apply for a Contracting Officer Warrant within 120 days of assignment and obtain it within 60 days of applying.
You must pass the USA Hire online assessment cut score and a background investigation, and show a REAL ID-compliant ID; Selective Service registration applies if male.
keywords: coordinates responses to external and internal audits
strategy: Before applying, honestly inventory whether at least 4 years of your work, including IEM, involved contracting or related duties and whether one year matched the GS-12 examples; if not, aim for GS-1102-07/09 trainee or Acquisition Intern roles instead.
Check your transcript for the 24 semester hours in the listed business fields and upload it, since a missing transcript can disqualify you.

If IEM work involved government contracts, frame it from the contractor side: proposal pricing, reviewing SOWs and deliverables against contract terms, task order management, compliance reporting, and audit responses, using the posting's wording.
On your two-page resume, list your title, month/year dates, and hours per week for every job, and give the specialized experience in short, specific bullets.
Answer the questionnaire only at levels your resume supports, because overstating can get you removed. Prepare for the USA Hire assessment, which has a cut score.
This is an open continuous announcement: the first referral cutoff is September 8, 2026, and later cutoffs come every two weeks through March 1, 2027, so apply early once your materials are accurate.
resume_bullets: Reviewed [number] [federal/state/local] contract task orders and statements of work valued at [$amount] for compliance with [FAR/contract terms], identifying [issues] and recommending [corrective actions].
Coordinated responses to [internal/external] audits and reviews of [program/contract] for [government client], preparing [reports/documentation] used by [audience] to [outcome].
Analyzed [cost/pricing or performance] data across [number] [contracts/projects], identified [trend], and prepared reports with action plans to meet [performance measures].
interview_questions: Walk us through how you would choose between simplified acquisition, sealed bidding, and negotiation for a given requirement.
Describe a time you found a compliance problem in a contract or deliverable and how you resolved it.
How would you prepare pre-negotiation objectives and decide that a price is fair and reasonable?
How would you mentor a less experienced Contract Specialist who is struggling with a complex procurement?
watch_outs: The degree, 24 semester hours, and 4 years of contracting experience are hard requirements, and waivers are rare and at agency discretion.
This is a warranted Contracting Officer role, so you must get a warrant within months and sign your own awards.
Work is on site at VA space under return-to-office rules, and the duty locations are listed as 'Multiple Locations.' Confirm a location within commuting range of Manassas before applying.
There is no promotion potential, no relocation pay, and a 1-year probationary period.
